            AI Supremacy 

SubscribeSign inProspectusGemini 2 and the rise of multi-modal AI 

Google's AI "product splurge" is about to get more fascinating in 2025. 

Michael SpencerDec 12, 2024∙ Paid67419ShareOn 26 January 2014, Google confirmed its acquisition of DeepMind for a price reportedly ranging between $400 million and $650 million. Ten years later and after dozens of AI startups have splintered out of Google Brain and Google Deepmind (now merged), and with the advent of Generative AI and ChatGPT, Google has been under pressure. 

In a seemingly heroic effort, Google has managed to embed Generative AI features in nearly all of their products and have a number of promising prototypes, including the now viral NotebookLM. Google, along with Amazon backed Anthropic and Microsoft backed OpenAI are among the world’s bleeding edge frontier LLM builders. 

Share

Google in the last couple of years have fiercely fought to win back talent, try to rethink their Search journey, leverage Generative AI for Google Cloud’s growth and significantly improve their products with Generative AI features. We think of OpenAI as one of the most prolific Generative AI product companies, but Google is often underestimated here. 

Now Google has released Gemini 2 along with new Realtime Multimodal API, powered by Gemini 2.0 Flash! Google has lowered the cost of LLMs and made them more accessible than ever before. The benchmarks also tell that story in terms of the performance of their Models.

Google’s Gemini 2 Release 

Google released the first version of its Gemini 2.0 family of artificial intelligence models on December 11th, 2024. Including its Chrome browser automation product called Mariner. 

Join the Waitlist

Project Astra and Mariner along with NotebookLM remain very intriguing AI products by Google in 2025. 

TechCrunch Google’s Generative AI product will come to fruition in 2025 in a way that will noticeably eclipse those of Microsoft, Meta, Amazon and Apple. 

Gemini 2.0 Flash, as the model is called, is available in a chat version for users globally while an experimental multimodal version of the model is available to developers.
